samples.summary: The newly centralized envelope rule is bypassed by ~25 sibling command sites that still flatten upstream bodies to `HTTP <status>`, including the client-synthesised SESSION_EXPIRED envelope
samples.evidence: `HttpClient` synthesises a real documented envelope on a dead refresh token — `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:157-164` returns `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED', message:'Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`.'}}` with status 401. Every command path that does NOT go through the new `forwardUpstreamError` discards it: `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25,65,91,143`, `commands/tabs.ts:16,49,75`, `commands/files.ts:86,106,124,142`, `commands/docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157`, `commands/notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117`, `commands/slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122`, `commands/api-keys.ts:18,32,46` all do `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`, so the user sees `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 401"}}` instead of the login guidance that `docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-cli-expired-session-404-todo.md:60-62` records as the invariant ("users still get a clear 'run `wafflebase login`' message when both tokens are gone"). `commands/sheets-export.ts:41` similarly casts rather than checks. This is pre-existing rather than introduced here, and the change's own non-goals defer `sheets cells`/`sheets export` (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:56-58) — but the same bypass exists well beyond sheets, so the acceptance criterion "every CLI path that prints an upstream body shares one guard" holds only for the six forwarding paths. The fix belongs on those out-of-diff sites (route them through `isErrorEnvelope`/`forwardUpstreamError`), not on the new helper.

finding.summary: Backend has no global exception filter, so every real server rejection on the newly-converted paths is Nest-shaped and now loses its message
finding.evidence: The backend never registers an ExceptionFilter (grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` across packages/backend/src returns nothing), so its rejections on exactly the endpoints these commands hit come back as Nest defaults `{message, error: 'Bad Request', statusCode}` — e.g. `packages/backend/src/file/file.controller.ts:35` (`new BadRequestException('No file uploaded')`) and `packages/backend/src/file/file.service.ts:106` (the size/type rejection). Those bodies fail `isErrorEnvelope`, so after this delta `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217`, `files/download.ts:57` and the six import sites print `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 400"}}` and drop the only human-readable reason the server gave. Before the delta the body was forwarded verbatim, so the reason survived. Only errors from an endpoint that already emits the `{error:{code}}` envelope keep their text; nothing in the backend does. Fix belongs on the new helper (`packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:128`): fold a framework body's `message` into the envelope's `message` rather than discarding it.

verdict.reason: The underlying facts check out — there is no global exception filter in packages/backend/src (main.ts:30-79 registers only pipes/CORS/body-parsers; grep for ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|@Catch is empty), so file.controller.ts:35 and file.service.ts:106 do produce Nest-default bodies whose `error` is the string 'Bad Request', which fails isErrorEnvelope (formatter.ts:76-85) and is collapsed to {"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 400"}} at formatter.ts:128-132. But this is not a blast-radius defect: no caller is left broken, no guard is bypassed, no export removed, no invariant violated. All 11 upstreamErrorJson consumers and 6 forwardUpstreamError consumers were migrated, and the emitted shape is exactly the contract the downstream consumers already document (packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84 and slides-import-pptx.md:72 promise HTTP_ERROR for server rejections; README.md:117 documents {error:{code,message}}). The behaviour is the task's explicit acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47), with backend error bodies listed as a non-goal (line 55), and the helper's own docstring (formatter.ts:112-122) anticipates framework bodies. The finding is statable purely from the diff and the reviewer places the fix on the new helper — that is the correctness/design-fit lane, not this one. The supporting claim "nothing in the backend" emits the envelope is also false: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42-47 emits {error:{code:'TYPE_MISMATCH',message:…}}. Residual impact is a lost prose string on an already-failing path with preserved exit code and status — minor, not blocking here.
